newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Leumi Q1 net up on one-time gains.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi Q1 net up on one-time gains.

text.p: Israel's Bank Leumi posted first-quarter net earnings of 618.3 million shekels, or 0.44 shekels a share, thanks to 456.2 million shekels in one-time gains from the sale of holdings in non-bank companies.
Leumi, Israel's second-largest bank, said income from ordinary operations came to 162.3 million shekels in the quarter, which still represented an increase of 46.2 percent from a year earlier.
Net annualised return on equity was 15 percent including the extraordinary items and 8.9 percent without them, compared with 6.4 percent in the year-earlier quarter, the bank said.

The gains were mainly from the sales of Leumi's holdings in Leumi Insurance Holdings and Africa-Israel Investments The sales were made to comply with new legislation requiring commercial banks to reduce their holdings in their non-bank businesses.
The bank announced in April it was paying a cash dividend of 452.6 million shekels on the gains to shareholders as of May 14.

Leumi's earnings were weighed down by an increase in the doubtful-debt provision to 170.3 million shekels from 81.2 million shekels a year ago. As a result, interest income after the provision was down 1.5 percent to 723.1 million shekels.
Leumi said it boosted the provision "against the backdrop of the slowdown in the economy and taking into consideration the one-time profit from the sale of excess share of non-bank holdings".
Operating and other income rose 5.6 percent from a year ago to 573.6 million shekels, Leumi said, while operating expenses declined 10.7 percent to 348.3 million shekels.

The bank said shareholders' equity grew 4.4 percent in the quarter and 8.2 percent on the year to 7.829 billion shekels as of March 31. Total assets came to 132.2 billion shekels, up 7.7 percent in the three months.

Credit to the public stood at 77.1 billion shekels as of March 31, up 1.8 percent for the quarter and 9.7 percent for the year. Deposits from the public were unchanged for the quarter at 109.5 billion shekels but up 9.6 percent on the year.
